claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure.
A reduced-order, machine-learning-enhanced framework can integrate the hierarchical heterostructural features of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed framework can predict Young's modulus for HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed framework can predict yield strength for HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed framework can predict fracture-related behavior for HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed framework will reduce computational time by approximately 50% relative to conventional full-field simulations.
The proposed framework will reduce mean predictive error by approximately 20% relative to conventional full-field simulations.
The relevant hierarchical heterostructure includes grain-boundary distributions.
The relevant hierarchical heterostructure includes phase morphology.
The relevant hierarchical heterostructure includes microscale reinforcement features.
Direct incorporation of measurable microstructural attributes enables machine-learning algorithms to capture the mediators of elastic deformation.
Direct incorporation of measurable microstructural attributes enables machine-learning algorithms to capture the mediators of yielding.
Direct incorporation of measurable microstructural attributes enables machine-learning algorithms to capture the mediators of crack propagation.
The proposed approach bypasses computationally intensive meshing required by established full-field simulations.
The proposed approach bypasses computationally intensive parameter sweeps required by established full-field simulations.
Prediction performance may deteriorate if detailed microstructural features cannot be quantified reliably.
The selected microstructural features may be insufficient if they do not capture dislocation dynamics, crack deflection, or phase-specific behavior governing macroscopic response.
Unpredictable processing-induced heterogeneity may reduce the reliability of model predictions.
